title: Machine-learned design of CuPd nanocubes for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia
summary: Interpretable machine learning identified ordered B2 CuPd intermetallics whose adsorption energies break the usual scaling relations. The team synthesized monodisperse CuPd nanocubes that reached a 92.5% Faradaic efficiency at -0.5 V RHE for nitrate reduction to ammonia, with a yield of 6.25 mol h-1 g-1 at -0.6 V. Performance was measured in the authors' own electrochemical tests, and the design rules come from a limited set of predicted intermetallics.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine learning on d-state Pauli repulsion descriptors (DFT-based)
organization: Virginia Tech; National University of Singapore; Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: The authors synthesized monodisperse ordered B2 CuPd nanocubes and measured nitrate reduction performance in their own electrochemical tests (92.5% Faradaic efficiency at -0.5 V RHE).
evidence.ai_role: Interpretable machine learning identified ordered B2 CuPd intermetallics whose adsorption energies break scaling relations and provided design rules.
